title: Cooperative Boundary Switching of Mesoscopic Real Spectra in a Non-Hermitian Chain Family
authors: Chengxi Li, Hao Zhu, Tie-Fu Zhang, Wanzi Sun, Wuming Li
abstract: At fixed bulk criticality, every fixed nonsingular real single-end potential preserves a growing local population of real eigenvalues in an open analytic family of non-Hermitian chains. An open region of two-end real potentials removes this population. A boundary-amplitude criterion fixes the minimum number of controlled ends. The population grows as $\sqrt N$, where $N$ is chain length, although its normalized spectral weight vanishes and the local limiting bands remain unchanged. For a representative chain's four zero-detuning settings, an independent passive Hermitian double chain converts this distinction into separated resonances at one fixed local port under a common coupling scan at fixed probe carrier. Its absolute reflection contrast and stability margin both scale as $N^{-1}$, with explicit sufficient resource budgets. Boundary amplitudes thus fix a minimum control requirement that limiting bands and thermodynamic spectral density do not specify.
summary: This theoretical work analyzes the spectral properties of non-Hermitian mesoscopic chains, focusing on the existence of a growing population of real eigenvalues. It proves that while single boundary controls cannot eliminate this spectrum, the cooperative control of two boundaries can achieve this, fixing a minimum control requirement independent of bulk spectral measurements. The methodology involves advanced spectral analysis techniques applied to open quantum systems.
main_problem: The paper investigates the cooperative boundary switching required to control and eliminate a growing, subextensive population of real eigenvalues in a non-Hermitian mesoscopic chain.
main_result: The population of real modes scales as $\sqrt{N}$ and is preserved by single-end potentials, but its removal requires the multiplicative control provided by two separated end potentials.
method: The analysis uses determinant calculations, input-output theory, and asymptotic analysis (like Rouché's theorem) to count and characterize the real eigenvalues of the non-Hermitian Hamiltonian.
model_or_system: The system is a non-interacting, open, non-Hermitian chain of $N$ sites, modeled by a specific Hamiltonian involving long-range hoppings and tunable boundary potentials ($v_L, v_R$).
key_observables: The count of real eigenvalues ($N_R$), reflection amplitude ($\varrho_N$), and the amplitude defect ($q_N$).
important_parameters: Chain length ($N$), boundary potentials ($v_L, v_R$), and the detuning/energy scan parameter ($E$).
main_assumptions: The analysis relies on asymptotic limits ($N \to \infty$) and specific error budgets for finite-size effects and calibration.
figures_summary: Figures compare the growing population of real modes under different boundary conditions (single vs. two ends) and show the scaling of reflection amplitudes and resonance counts versus energy scan parameters.
paper_structure: The paper progresses from establishing the existence of the $\sqrt{N}$ real spectrum preserved by single boundaries, to demonstrating that two boundaries are necessary for closure, and finally analyzing the spectral robustness and finite-size error bounds.
why_interesting: This work provides rigorous mathematical tools for controlling spectral properties in open, non-Hermitian quantum systems, which is highly relevant for quantum optics and open quantum systems research.
